lines: (Nobody ever got hurt yet is not a safety record.)
So the third harmonic is…
That pin is what keeps someone safe if something inside fails. We don't trade it for quiet.
Not the adapter. Two grounded systems disagreeing a little. The grounds are fine — the hum rides the signal path.
That's going on a mug.
The building was fine. It just needed a translator.
(It was not her. It was never going to be her.)
Sing again? …Channel 7. You're on 7. The lectern's on 3.
What changed Tuesday?
Priya photographed every cable. A month ago. Only 3 and 7 moved.
And a label?
Nobody checked the middle after, remember? Nobody checked the patch after.
You label your mug.
You labeled your label maker.
Thanks for telling me first. Which outlets are those on?
(Nobody laughs. Then everybody does. Then the stage stays dark.)
Sofia, take the lights to zero at the desk. Everyone off the stage-left gear. Nobody plugs anything anywhere.
And the breaker?
It tripped because we asked too much of it. If we reset it and I'm wrong about why, we find out the hard way.
Stage-left breaker tripped at 7:41 when twelve new fixtures went to full. My estimate: about 2,700 watts on it. Nothing's been opened or reset.
Was that good or bad?
Know versus do.
Next time, bring me the look and I'll bring Andre the table.
